long_biography.plain_text:
Jim Baum earned a mechanical-engineering degree at Cornell, rowed varsity heavyweight crew and gained both a pilot's license and an Air Force commission while still a student. Graduate study in aeronautical engineering followed at Stanford. He then flew transport and reconnaissance aircraft in Vietnam, receiving the Distinguished Flying Cross, before continuing his aviation career with the Federal Aviation Administration.

Returning to Southern California, Baum managed Dwight C. Baum Investments and later became known publicly as a private investor. His connection to USC Viterbi began when his son helped create the university's Formula SAE racing team. Baum supported the students, went on to chair the school's Board of Councilors and helped establish a maker space designed specifically for undergraduate building, testing and competition projects.
